title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 18th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en: 1. An ongoing act of unlawfully restricting another person's personal freedom shall be considered an 'unlawful infringement' as stipulated in Paragraph 1 of Article 20 of the Criminal Law, and justifiable defense may be exercised. 2. An act of unlawfully restricting another person's personal freedom accompanied by insult and minor beating shall not be considered a 'violent crime seriously endangering personal safety' as stipulated in Paragraph 3 of Article 20 of the Criminal Law. 3. In determining whether defense exceeds the limits of necessity, consideration shall be given comprehensively to the nature, means, intensity, and degree of harm of the unlawful infringement, as well as the nature, timing, means, intensity, environment, and consequences of the defensive act. For an unlawful infringement that involves unlawfully restricting another person's personal freedom accompanied by insult and minor beating and is not particularly imminent, if the defense causes death or severe injury, it shall be considered as 'clearly exceeding the limits of necessity causing major harm' as stipulated in Paragraph 2 of Article 20 of the Criminal Law. 4. In cases of excessive defense, if the case is triggered by the victim's unlawful infringement that seriously demeans another person's human dignity or violates human ethics, full consideration shall be given to this factor at sentencing to ensure that the judicial judgment not only withstands legal scrutiny but also conforms to social concepts of fairness and justice.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the 18th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2018] No. 164

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the four cases, including the case of Yu Huan for intentional injury (Guiding Cases No. 93-96), are hereby issued as the 18th batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

June 20, 2018

Guiding Case No. 93

Yu Huan v. [No party listed] — intentional injury case

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and issued on June 20, 2018)

Keywords: criminal / intentional injury / unlawful restriction of personal freedom / justifiable defense / excessive defense

Ruling Gist

1. Conduct that unlawfully restricts another person's personal freedom while it is ongoing shall be deemed "unlawful infringement" as provided in Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, and may be subject to justifiable defense.

2. Conduct that unlawfully restricts another person's personal freedom, accompanied by insults or minor beatings, shall not be deemed "a violent crime seriously endangering personal safety" as provided in Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law.

3. In determining whether defense is excessive, consideration shall be given comprehensively to the nature, means, intensity, and degree of harm of the unlawful infringement, as well as the nature, timing, means, intensity, environment, and harmful consequences of the defensive act, among other circumstances. Where the unlawful infringement consists of unlawful restriction of personal freedom accompanied by insults or minor beatings, and is not extremely imminent, a defensive act that results in death or serious injury shall be deemed to have "clearly exceeded the necessary limits and caused major harm" as provided in Article 20, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law.

4. In cases of excessive defense, if the case is triggered by the victim's unlawful infringement that seriously derogates from another's human dignity or violates human ethics, full consideration shall be given to this factor at sentencing, to ensure that the judicial decision withstands legal scrutiny and conforms to society's concepts of fairness and justice.

Relevant Legal Provision

Article 20 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The mother of the defendant Yu Huan, Su Mou, operated Shandong Yuanda Industry and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuanda Company) in Guan County Industrial Park, Shandong Province. Yu Huan was an employee of the company. On July 28, 2014, Su Mou and her husband, Yu Mou 1, borrowed RMB 1,000,000 from Wu Mou and Zhao Mou 1, with an oral agreement on a monthly interest rate of 10%. By October 20, 2015, Su Mou had repaid a total of RMB 1,540,000. During this period, because Su Mou's repayments were not timely, Wu Mou and Zhao Mou 1 instructed the victim Guo Mou 1, among others, to take measures such as camping in the company's bicycle shed and cooking in front of the office building to press for debt repayment. On November 1, 2015, Su Mou and Yu Mou 1 borrowed an additional RMB 350,000 from Wu Mou and Zhao Mou 1. For RMB 100,000 of this amount, the parties orally agreed on a monthly interest rate of 10%; for the remaining RMB 250,000, a house sales contract was signed, using a house under Yu Mou 1's name as collateral, with the agreement that if repayment was overdue, the house would be transferred to Zhao Mou 1. From November 2, 2015 to January 6, 2016, Su Mou repaid a total of RMB 298,000 to Zhao Mou 1. Wu Mou and Zhao Mou 1 considered this RMB 298,000 to be repayment of interest on the first loan of RMB 1,000,000, while Su Mou and her husband believed it was repayment of the second loan. Wu Mou and Zhao Mou 1 repeatedly urged Su Mou and her husband to continue repayment or to handle the house transfer procedures, but they neither repaid further nor handled the house transfer.

On April 1, 2016, Zhao Mou 1, together with the victims Du Mou 2 and Guo Mou 1, among others, changed the locks on the aforementioned house of Yu Mou 1 and forcibly moved in. Su Mou called the police. Zhao Mou 1 presented the house sales contract, and the police mediated before leaving. On the morning of the 13th of the same month, Wu Mou, Zhao Mou 1, Du Mou 2, Guo Mou 1, Du Mou 7, and others moved items out of the aforementioned house. Su Mou called the police. When the police arrived, Wu Mou claimed it was a house sales dispute, and the police informed the parties to negotiate or resolve it through litigation. After the police left, Wu Mou scolded Su Mou and pressed her head into the toilet bowl near the water surface. That afternoon, Zhao Mou 1 and others moved the items from the house to the entrance of Yuanda Company. During this time, Su Mou and Yu Mou 1 repeatedly called the mayor's hotline for help. That evening, Yu Mou 1, through mediation by others, reached an oral agreement with Wu Mou, agreeing to transfer the house to Zhao Mou 1 the next day, and then pay an additional RMB 300,000, after which the principal and interest on the loan would be fully settled.

On April 14, Yu Mou 1 and Su Mou did not go to handle the house transfer procedures. At approximately 4:00 p.m. on the same day, Zhao Mou 1 gathered Guo Mou 2, Guo Mou 1, Miao Mou, and Zhang Mou 3 to go to Yuanda Company to demand repayment. To find Yu Mou 1 and Su Mou, Guo Mou 1 called the police, falsely claiming that Yuanda Company had privately engraved a financial seal. Upon the police's arrival at Yuanda Company, Su Mou argued with Zhao Mou 1 and others over the repayment dispute. The police informed the parties to resolve the matter through negotiation or to file a lawsuit, and then left. After receiving a call from Zhao Mou 1, Li Mou 3, together with Yao Mou, Zhang Mou 2, and the victims Yan Mou and Cheng Mou, arrived at Yuanda Company. Zhao Mou 1 and others shouted in front of the office building, kept watch inside the finance office and outside the dining hall, and barbecued and drank alcohol outside the office building foyer, urging Su Mou to repay. During this time, Zhao Mou 1 and Miao Mou left. At approximately 8:00 p.m., Du Mou 2 and Du Mou 7 arrived at Yuanda Company and drank alcohol with Li Mou 3 and others. At 8:48 p.m., Su Mou, upon Guo Mou 1's request, went to the reception room on the first floor of the office building, accompanied by Yu Huan and company employees Zhang Mou 1 and Ma Mou. At 9:53 p.m., Du Mou 2 and others entered the reception room to demand repayment, taking away the mobile phones of Su Mou and Yu Huan and placing them on the office desk. Du Mou 2 used obscene language to insult Su Mou, Yu Huan, and their family; flicked a cigarette butt onto the clothes on Su Mou's chest; pulled down his pants to his thighs, exposing his genitals; and twisted his body left and right in front of Su Mou and others sitting on the sofa. After being dissuaded by Ma Mou and Li Mou 3, Du Mou 2 pulled up his pants, then took off Yu Huan's shoes and made Su Mou smell them, which Su Mou knocked away. Du Mou 2 also slapped Yu Huan's face, and other debt collectors pulled Yu Huan's hair or pressed his shoulders to prevent him from standing up. At 10:07 p.m., company employee Liu Mou called the police. At 10:17 p.m., police officer Zhu Mou, together with auxiliary police officers Song Mou and Guo Mou 3, arrived at the reception room of Yuanda Company to check the situation. Su Mou and Yu Huan pointed out that Du Mou 2 had beaten Yu Huan; Du Mou 2 and others denied this, claiming they were collecting a debt. At 10:22 p.m., Zhu Mou warned both sides not to fight, then led the auxiliary police to the yard to look for the person who called the police, and called the duty officer Xu Mou to report the situation. Yu Huan and Su Mou wanted to leave the reception room with the police, but Du Mou 2 and others blocked them and forced Yu Huan to sit down; Yu Huan refused. Du Mou 2 and others grabbed Yu Huan's neck and pushed and pulled him to the southeast corner of the reception room. Yu Huan, holding a single-edged pointed knife with a blade length of 15.3 cm, warned Du Mou 2 and others not to come closer. Du Mou 2 taunted him and approached, whereupon Yu Huan stabbed Du Mou 2 once in the abdomen, and then stabbed Cheng Mou in the chest, Yan Mou in the abdomen, and Guo Mou 1 in the back, once each. At 10:26 p.m., the auxiliary police officer, hearing the noise, returned to the reception room. After repeated orders from the auxiliary police, Yu Huan handed over the knife. Du Mou 2 and three others, injured, were driven by Du Mou 7 and others to Guan County People's Hospital for treatment. At 2:18 a.m. the next day, Du Mou 2 died despite rescue efforts, due to hemorrhagic shock caused by a laceration of the proper hepatic artery and a wound to the right lobe of the liver from the abdominal injury. The injuries to Yan Mou and Guo Mou 1 both constituted second-degree serious injuries, and the injury to Cheng Mou constituted second-degree minor injury.

Judgment

The Intermediate People's Court of Liaocheng City, Shandong Province, on February 17, 2017, rendered the criminal附带 civil judgment (2016) Lu 15 Xing Chu No. 33, finding the defendant Yu Huan guilty of intentional injury, sentencing him to life imprisonment, depriving him of political rights for life, and ordering him to compensate the附带 civil plaintiffs for economic losses.

After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Yu Huan and some of the original附带 civil plaintiffs, dissatisfied, filed appeals respectively. The High People's Court of Shandong Province, after trial, on June 23, 2017, rendered the criminal附带 civil judgment (2017) Lu Xing Zhong No. 151: dismissed the appeals on the附带 civil part, affirming the original judgment on that part; reversed the criminal part of the original judgment, and changed the sentence to five years' imprisonment for the crime of intentional injury.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: The act of the defendant Yu Huan in stabbing Du Mou 2 and three others was aimed at stopping ongoing unlawful infringement, and thus had a defensive nature; his defensive act resulted in one death, two serious injuries, and one minor injury, clearly exceeding the necessary limits and causing major harm, constituting the crime of intentional injury, for which he should bear criminal responsibility. Given that Yu Huan's act constituted excessive defense, that Yu Huan truthfully confessed the main crimes after being brought to justice, and that the victim side had serious fault, including insulting Yu Huan's mother by despicable means, Yu Huan should be given a mitigated punishment in accordance with law. The original judgment correctly found Yu Huan guilty of intentional injury, and the trial procedure was lawful, but the factual findings were incomplete, some criminal sentencing items applied the law incorrectly, and the penalty was too severe; therefore, the sentence was changed to five years' imprisonment in accordance with law.

The main issues in dispute in the application of law in this case are mainly two: first, the nature of Yu Huan's stabbing act, i.e., whether it had a defensive nature, whether it constituted special defense, and whether it constituted excessive defense; second, how to convict and impose punishment.

I. Regarding the nature of Yu Huan's stabbing act

Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law) provides: "An act that is taken to stop an ongoing unlawful infringement that endangers the State, the public interest, or the personal, property, or other rights of oneself or another person, and that causes harm to the infringer, constitutes justifiable defense and the actor shall not bear criminal responsibility." It follows that the establishment of justifiable defense must simultaneously satisfy the following five conditions: First, the cause of defense: the unlawful infringement must exist in reality. Unlawful infringement refers to an invasion or harm that violates the law, including both criminal acts and general illegal acts; it includes both acts infringing on personal rights and acts infringing on property and other rights. Second, the timing of defense: the unlawful infringement must be ongoing. "Ongoing" means the period during which the unlawful infringement has already begun and has not yet ended. An unlawful infringement that has not yet begun or has already ended cannot be defended against; otherwise, the defense is untimely. Third, the object of defense: the defense must be directed at the infringer himself. The object of justifiable defense can only be the infringer himself, and cannot be persons other than the infringer. In the case of joint unlawful infringement, the joint infringement is integral, and justifiable defense may be exercised against each joint infringer. Fourth, the intent of defense: there must be an intent to stop the unlawful infringement, with defensive awareness and will. Fifth, the limits of defense: the defense must not clearly exceed the necessary limits and cause major harm. That is to say, the conditions for the establishment of justifiable defense include objective conditions, subjective conditions, and conditions of limits. The objective and subjective conditions are qualitative conditions, which determine the "righteous" nature and prerequisites of justifiable defense; if these conditions are not met, it is not justifiable defense. The condition of limits is a quantitative condition, which determines the requirement of "appropriateness" and reasonable limits of justifiable defense; if this condition is not met, the act still has a defensive nature but does not constitute justifiable defense, but rather excessive defense. An act of excessive defense has the prerequisite conditions of defense and the purpose of stopping unlawful infringement, but in the process of stopping the unlawful infringement, it fails to reasonably control the intensity of the defensive act, clearly exceeds the necessary limits of justifiable defense, and causes unjustified major harmful consequences, thereby transforming into an illegal or criminal act harmful to society. Based on the facts and evidence found in this case and the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law of China, Yu Huan's stabbing act, although having a defensive nature, constitutes excessive defense.

First, Yu Huan's stabbing act had a defensive nature. At the time of the incident, Du Mou 2 and others were continuously carrying out the unlawful detention of Yu Huan and Su Mou, restricting their personal freedom, accompanied by insults to their dignity, and acts such as pushing and slapping Yu Huan. When the police arrived at the scene, Yu Huan and Su Mou wanted to leave the reception room with the police, but Du Mou 2 and others prevented them from leaving, pushing, pulling, and encircling Yu Huan; when Yu Huan warned them with the knife, they still taunted and approached him. The unlawful infringement required for justifiable defense objectively existed and was ongoing. Yu Huan stabbed the knife when his personal freedom was unlawfully infringed and his personal safety faced a real threat, and the targets of his stabbing were all those who approached and encircled him after his warning. Therefore, it can be found that his act was taken to stop the ongoing unlawful infringement against the personal rights of himself and his mother, satisfying the objective and subjective conditions of justifiable defense, and having a defensive nature.

Second, Yu Huan's stabbing act did not constitute special defense. Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law provides: "If a person takes a defensive act against ongoing violent crimes of assault, murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, or other violent crimes seriously endangering personal safety, causing injury or death to the unlawful infringer, it is not excessive defense, and the actor shall not bear criminal responsibility." According to this provision, the prerequisite for the application of special defense is the existence of a violent crime seriously endangering the personal safety of the actor or another person. In this case, although Du Mou 2 and others committed personal infringement acts such as unlawful restriction of personal freedom, insults, and minor beatings against Yu Huan and his mother, these unlawful infringements were not violent crimes seriously endangering personal safety. First, the unlawful infringements of unlawful restriction of personal freedom and insults committed by Du Mou 2 and others, although infringing on the lawful rights and interests of Yu Huan and his mother, such as personal freedom and human dignity, did not have the nature of seriously endangering the personal safety of Yu Huan and his mother. Second, the compulsory or beating acts such as pressing shoulders, pushing, and pulling by Du Mou 2 and others, although infringing on the personal safety and right to health of Yu Huan and his mother, were only minor violent infringements; they were neither infringements against the right to life nor situations of serious infringement on the right to health of Yu Huan and his mother, and therefore did not constitute violent crimes seriously endangering personal safety. Third, Su Mou and Yu Mou 1 voluntarily borrowed money from Wu Mou through coordination and guarantee by others, and voluntarily accepted the 10% monthly interest proposed by Wu Mou. There was no fact that Su Mou or Yu Mou 1 was forced to borrow at high interest from Wu Mou, nor was there any fact that Wu Mou forced Su Mou or Yu Mou 1 to borrow, which is clearly inconsistent with the judicial interpretation that obtaining others' property by violence or coercion under the guise of a loan constitutes robbery. It can be seen that the various unlawful infringements committed by Du Mou 2 and others met the prerequisite conditions for exercising general defense, but did not meet the prerequisite conditions for special defense; therefore, Yu Huan's stabbing act did not constitute special defense.

Finally, Yu Huan's stabbing act constituted excessive defense. Article 20, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law provides: "If justifiable defense clearly exceeds the necessary limits and causes major harm, the actor shall bear criminal responsibility, but the punishment shall be mitigated or exempted." It follows that excessive defense occurs when, under the objective and subjective prerequisite conditions of justifiable defense, the defensive counterattack clearly exceeds the necessary limits and causes the excessive result of serious injury or death. Whether defense "clearly exceeds the necessary limits" shall be determined by comprehensive analysis of the nature, means, intensity, and degree of harm of the unlawful infringement, as well as the nature, timing, means, intensity, environment, and harmful consequences of the defensive act, among other factors. In this case, although Du Mou 2's side had a larger number of people, the intent of their unlawful infringement was to put pressure on Su Mou and her husband to push for debt repayment; they did not carry or use any instruments during the debt collection. Before the police officer Zhu Mou and others entered the reception room, Du Mou 2's side committed acts of unlawful restriction of personal freedom, insults, slapping Yu Huan's face, and pulling his hair against Yu Huan and his mother, with the purpose of forcing Su Mou and her husband to repay as soon as possible. When the police entered the reception room, there was no intense confrontation or physical conflict between the two sides. After the police warned them not to fight, Du Mou 2's side had no words or actions of fighting. While the police had left the reception room to find the person who called the police, both Yu Huan and the debt collectors could clearly see the flashing police lights of the patrol car parked in the yard through the glass of the reception room; they should have known that the police had not left. When Yu Huan warned them not to come closer while holding the knife, Du Mou 2 and others, although they taunted and approached him, did not carry out any violent attacks. Therefore, the unlawful infringement faced by Yu Huan was not urgent or serious, yet he used a single-edged pointed knife with a blade length of 15.3 cm to stab four people consecutively, causing one death, two serious injuries, and one minor injury, and one of them was stabbed in the back. Therefore, it should be found that Yu Huan's defensive act clearly exceeded the necessary limits and caused major harm, constituting excessive defense.

II. Regarding conviction and sentencing

First, regarding conviction. In this case, Yu Huan stabbed four people consecutively, but the targets of his stabbing were all those who were surrounding and approaching him at the time; he did not stab other unlawful infringers who were farther away; he stabbed each unlawful infringer once, and did not stab the same unlawful infringer consecutively. It can be seen that Yu Huan's purpose was to stop the unlawful infringement and leave the reception room; the evidence in the case cannot confirm that he had the intent to pursue or allow the harmful result of death to occur. Therefore, Yu Huan's act does not constitute intentional homicide. However, in order to achieve the effect of defense, he adopted an indifferent attitude toward the occurrence of the excessive result of multiple casualties, which already constitutes the crime of intentional injury under the circumstance of excessive defense. Finding Yu Huan's act to constitute the crime of intentional injury is not only a requirement of strict justice but also conforms to the people's concept of fairness and justice.

Second, regarding sentencing. Article 20, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law provides: "If justifiable defense clearly exceeds the necessary limits and causes major harm, the actor shall bear criminal responsibility, but the punishment shall be mitigated or exempted." Taking into comprehensive consideration the nature of the rights and interests protected by the defense, the method of defense, the intensity of defense, the cause of defense, the harmful consequences, the degree of excessiveness, the surrounding environment, and other circumstances, Yu Huan should be given a mitigated punishment.

The victim side had serious fault in triggering this case. Before the incident, Wu Mou and Zhao Mou 1 had instructed Du Mou 2 and others to commit debt collection acts including insulting Su Mou and disrupting the production and operation of Yuanda Company. Su Mou had called the police multiple times, but the unlawful debt collection acts of Wu Mou and others did not cease. On the day of the incident, Du Mou 2 and others committed acts of unlawful restriction of personal freedom, insults, and intermittent pushing, slapping, and neck grabbing against Yu Huan and Su Mou. Yu Huan and his mother Su Mou had been repeatedly subjected to urging, harassment, and insults for several consecutive days, which inevitably led Yu Huan to have emotions such as fear and anger when carrying out the defensive act. In particular, Du Mou 2's act of exposing his genitals to insult Su Mou constituted a major fault in triggering the case. On the day of the incident, Du Mou 2 exposed his genitals in front of Yu Huan to insult his mother Su Mou. Although approximately twenty minutes had passed before Yu Huan carried out the defensive act, it was inevitable that Yu Huan stabbed Du Mou 2 and others with some emotion of revenge against Du Mou 2 for insulting his mother; therefore, Du Mou 2's act of exposing his genitals to insult Su Mou was an important factor in triggering the case, and should be considered as a circumstance favorable to Yu Huan at the sentencing stage.

Du Mou 2's act of insulting Yu Huan's mother was seriously illegal and against human ethics, and should be punished and condemned. However, in a situation where the police were still investigating at the scene and the police car was still flashing lights in the yard, Yu Huan, in order to leave the reception room and escape encirclement, stabbed four people consecutively with a knife, causing one death, two serious injuries, and one minor injury; one of the seriously injured was stabbed in the back by Yu Huan. The harmful consequences were serious. Apart from Du Mou 2, the other three did not commit acts of insulting Yu Huan's mother. The harm caused by the defensive act far exceeded the lawful rights and interests protected, and the defense was clearly excessive. The personal freedom and human dignity of Yu Huan and his mother should be protected by law, but Yu Huan's defensive act clearly exceeded the necessary limits and caused serious consequences of multiple casualties, exceeding the limits permitted by law, and he should bear criminal responsibility in accordance with law.

According to the criminal law of China, anyone who intentionally causes injury resulting in death shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death; if the act constitutes excessive defense, the punishment shall be reduced or remitted. As stated above, Yu Huan's act of defense clearly exceeded the necessary limit and caused serious casualties; thus, in accordance with the law, the punishment shall be reduced and the sentence shall be imposed within the statutory sentencing range of three to ten years of fixed-term imprisonment. Given that Yu Huan truthfully confessed the main facts of the crime after being brought to justice, and that the victim side had serious fault in insulting Yu Huan's mother by despicable means, which constitutes a circumstance for lighter punishment, and taking into comprehensive consideration the facts, nature, circumstances, and harmful consequences of Yu Huan's crime, Yu Huan was sentenced to five years of fixed-term imprisonment.

(Trial judges for the effective judgment: Wu Jing, Liu Zhenhui, Wang Wenxing)

Guiding Case No. 94

Chongqing Fuling Zhida Property Management Co., Ltd. v.

Chongqing Fuling District Human Resources and Social Security Bureau

— administrative confirmation of labor and social security

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on June 20, 2018)

Keywords: administrative / administrative confirmation / deemed work-related injury / act of bravery for a just cause

Ruling Gist

Where an employee is injured while acting bravely for a just cause to stop illegal or criminal acts, such injury falls under the circumstance of being injured in safeguarding public interests as provided in Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 15 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, and shall be deemed as a work-related injury.

Related Legal Provisions

Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 15 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance

Basic Facts

Luo Renjun was a security guard employed by Chongqing Fuling Zhida Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fuling Zhida Property Company). On December 24, 2011, Luo Renjun was on duty (24-hour shift) at the Circle Dream Garden community served by Fuling Zhida Property Company. At approximately 8:30 a.m., near Hongfu Building on Xinghua Middle Road, someone was robbing a passerby. Hearing the shouts, Luo Renjun immediately stopped the robber's escape route and demanded the return of the stolen items. During the struggle with the robber, he accidentally fell from a 22-step staircase onto the platform at the corner of the alley and was injured. On June 12, 2012, Luo Renjun applied to the defendant, Chongqing Fuling District Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Fuling District HRSS Bureau), for a work-related injury confirmation. The Fuling District HRSS Bureau accepted the application on the same day and, on June 13, 2012, issued a Notice of Suspension of Work-Related Injury Confirmation to Luo Renjun, requesting him to supplement materials confirming his act as one of bravery for a just cause. On July 20, 2012, Luo Renjun submitted relevant materials on his act of bravery. After verification, the Fuling District HRSS Bureau, in accordance with Item 7 of Article 14 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, issued a Decision on Confirmation of Work-Related Injury (Fu Ren She Shang Xian Ren Jue Zi [2012] No. 676) on August 9, 2012, determining that Luo Renjun's injury was work-related. Dissatisfied, Fuling Zhida Property Company filed an administrative lawsuit. During the proceedings, the Fuling District HRSS Bureau issued a Decision to Revoke the Work-Related Injury Confirmation and, on June 25, 2013, in accordance with Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 15 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, issued a Decision on Confirmation of Work-Related Injury (Fu Ren She Shang Xian Ren Jue Zi [2013] No. 524), determining that Luo Renjun's injury was deemed work-related. Still dissatisfied, Fuling Zhida Property Company applied for administrative reconsideration to the Chongqing Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau on July 15, 2013. On August 21, 2013, the Chongqing Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau issued an Administrative Reconsideration Decision (Yu Ren She Fu Jue Zi [2013] No. 129), upholding the decision. Fuling Zhida Property Company argued that the Fuling District HRSS Bureau's determination was legally erroneous and that Luo Renjun's injury should not be recognized as work-related. Therefore, it filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting the revocation of the Decision on Confirmation of Work-Related Injury and an order for the defendant to make a new determination.

It was further established that the Social Management Comprehensive Governance Committee of Fuling District, Chongqing, commended Luo Renjun's act and issued a Notice on Commending Comrade Luo Renjun's Act of Bravery for a Just Cause (Fu Zong Zhi Wei Fa [2012] No. 5).

Judgment

The Fuling District People's Court of Chongqing rendered an administrative judgment (Fu Fa Xing Chu Zi [2013] No. 00077) on September 23, 2013, dismissing the lawsuit of Chongqing Fuling Zhida Property Management Co., Ltd. requesting the revocation of the Decision on Confirmation of Work-Related Injury (Fu Ren She Shang Xian Ren Jue Zi [2013] No. 524) made by the defendant. After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment has now taken legal effect.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: The defendant, Fuling District HRSS Bureau, is the county-level competent administrative department for labor. According to the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 5 of the State Council's Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, it has the administrative authority to accept applications for work-related injury confirmation within its administrative region and to determine whether an injury is work-related based on facts and law. Based on the Notice on Commending Comrade Luo Renjun's Act of Bravery for a Just Cause issued by the Social Management Comprehensive Governance Committee of Fuling District, Chongqing, provided by the third party Luo Renjun, the defendant determined that Luo Renjun was injured in the course of acting bravely for a just cause. The facts are clear and the evidence is sufficient. Luo Renjun, disregarding personal safety, fought against illegal and criminal acts, thereby protecting others' personal property and lives, maintaining social security order, and promoting social justice. The law should strongly advocate and encourage acts of bravery for a just cause.

Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 15 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance stipulates: "An employee who is injured in the course of rescuing others in emergencies or disasters, or in activities safeguarding national interests or public interests, shall be deemed to have suffered a work-related injury." Accordingly, even if the employee is not injured at the workplace or due to work reasons, if the injury is sustained in activities safeguarding national interests or public interests, it shall be treated as a work-related injury. Acts of bravery by citizens in fighting against illegal or criminal acts, similar to rescuing others in emergencies or disasters, are acts safeguarding public interests and should be strongly advocated and encouraged. Injuries sustained due to acts of bravery in stopping illegal or criminal acts shall be governed by the provisions of Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 15 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, i.e., deemed as work-related injuries.

Moreover, the Regulations of Chongqing Municipality on Encouraging Acts of Bravery for a Just Cause, a local regulation of Chongqing, further clarifies in Articles 19 and 21 that injuries from acts of bravery for a just cause shall be deemed as work-related injuries and entitled to work-related injury benefits. The above provisions of this regulation are consistent with the legislative intent of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, help to maximize the protection of劳动者的 legitimate rights and interests, and maximize the promotion of social justice, and shall be applied in this case.

In summary, the defendant, Fuling District HRSS Bureau, correctly applied the law in determining that Luo Renjun's injury was deemed work-related.

(Trial judges for the effective judgment: Liu Yun, Chen Qijuan, Yang Zhongmin)

Guiding Case No. 95

Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd.

Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch v. Xuancheng Baiguan Trading

Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Kaisheng Real Estate Co., Ltd., et al.

— dispute over financial loan contract

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on June 20, 2018)

Keywords: civil / financial loan contract / guarantee / ceiling mortgage

Ruling Gist

Where the parties reach a separate agreement to include a pre-existing creditor's right, which arose before the establishment of a ceiling mortgage, within the scope of the creditor's rights secured by that ceiling mortgage, as long as the amount of the included creditor's right remains within the maximum amount limit secured by the ceiling mortgage, even if no modification registration has been made for the ceiling mortgage, the validity of the ceiling mortgage still extends to the included creditor's right, provided that no adverse effect is caused to third parties.

Related Legal Provisions

Articles 203 and 205 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On April 20, 2012, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd., Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch) entered into a Small Enterprise Loan Contract with Xuancheng Baiguan Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baiguan Company), agreeing that Baiguan Company would borrow RMB 3,000,000 from ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch, with a loan term of seven months from the actual drawdown date: RMB 1,000,000 to be repaid on November 1, 2012, and RMB 2,000,000 to be repaid on November 17, 2012. The contract also stipulated the loan interest rate, deposit, etc. On April 24, 2012, ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch disbursed the above loan to Baiguan Company.

On October 16, 2012, the shareholders' meeting of Jiangsu Kaisheng Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kaisheng Company) resolved to mortgage the property located at No. 118, Jiangshan Avenue, Suyu District, Suqian City, Jiangsu Province - Suqian Hongxing Kaisheng International Home Furnishing Plaza (room number: B-201, property right certificate number: Su Yu Di Quan Zheng [2011] No. 104767) to ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch as security for the financing of four enterprises, namely Baiguan Company, Minhang Company, Hangjia Company, and Jinyida Company, which were tenants of Yirongda Company, at ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch. Any economic disputes arising therefrom would be borne by Kaisheng Company. On October 23, 2012, Kaisheng Company issued a commitment letter for property mortgage guarantee to ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch, agreeing to provide the above property as mortgage security for the financing of the above four enterprises at ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch, and promising that if any of these four enterprises failed to repay the debts of ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch on time, and if the value of the mortgaged property after disposal was insufficient to cover all debts, Kaisheng Company would use other property to repay the remaining debts. This commitment letter and the above shareholders' meeting resolution were signed by all shareholders of Kaisheng Company and affixed with the company's seal. On October 24, 2012, ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch and Kaisheng Company entered into a Ceiling Mortgage Contract, agreeing that Kaisheng Company would use the shop property under the real estate title certificate (Su Fang Quan Zheng Su Yu Zi [2011] No. 104767) to provide mortgage security for the claims of ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch against the debtors arising from loan contracts entered into with Baiguan Company, Minhang Company, Hangjia Company, and Jinyida Company during the period from October 19, 2012 to October 19, 2015, within a maximum balance of RMB 40,000,000, regardless of whether such claims had matured at the expiration of the above period or whether such claims had arisen before the establishment of the ceiling mortgage. The security scope included the principal, interest, and costs of enforcing claims. On the same day, the parties registered the mortgage for the property in accordance with the law, and ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch obtained a real estate mortgage certificate (Su Fang Ta Zheng Su Yu Di [2012] No. 201204387). On November 3, 2012, Kaisheng Company again passed a shareholders' meeting resolution and issued a commitment letter for property mortgage guarantee to ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch, the contents and signatures/seals of which were identical to the previous ones. On the same day, Kaisheng Company and ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch entered into a Supplementary Agreement, clarifying that the security scope of the Ceiling Mortgage Contract entered into between the parties included the claims under the four loan contracts signed between ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch and Baiguan Company, Minhang Company, Hangjia Company, and Jinyida Company on April 20, 2012.

Baiguan Company failed to repay the loan on time, and ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the Xuancheng Intermediate People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering Baiguan Company to repay the loan principal, interest, and costs of enforcing claims, and requiring Kaisheng Company to assume mortgage liability with the property under the real estate title certificate (Su Fang Quan Zheng Su Yu Zi [2011] No. 104767).

Judgment

The Xuancheng Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment (Xuan Zhong Min Er Chu Zi [2013] No. 00080) on November 10, 2013: 1. Baiguan Company shall pay ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch the loan principal of RMB 3,000,000 and interest within five days of the judgment taking effect. ... 4. If Baiguan Company fails to perform the payment obligation under the above item 1 within the period specified in the judgment, ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch shall have the right to seek priority in repayment by way of discounting the property under the real estate title certificate (Su Fang Quan Zheng Su Yu Zi [2011] No. 104767) provided by Kaisheng Company, or from the proceeds of the auction or sale of the property... After the judgment was pronounced, Kaisheng Company appealed to the Anhui High People's Court, arguing that the matter stipulated in the Supplementary Agreement had not been registered for modification of the ceiling mortgage. The Anhui High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (Wan Min Er Zhong Zi [2014] No. 00395) on October 21, 2014, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: Kaisheng Company and ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch entered into the Ceiling Mortgage Contract on October 24, 2012, agreeing that Kaisheng Company would voluntarily use its property as mortgage to provide ceiling mortgage security for the loan principal and interest borrowed by Baiguan Company from ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch during the period from October 19, 2012 to October 19, 2015, within a maximum balance of RMB 40,000,000, and the mortgage was registered. ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch lawfully obtained the mortgage over the property. On November 3, 2012, Kaisheng Company and ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch further entered into a Supplementary Agreement, stipulating that the principal claims secured by the aforementioned ceiling mortgage contract include the claims under the Small Enterprise Loan Contract signed between ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch and Baiguan Company on April 20, 2012. This Supplementary Agreement was signed and sealed by both parties and was consistent with the shareholders' meeting resolution of Kaisheng Company and the commitment letter for property mortgage guarantee it issued. Therefore, the Supplementary Agreement represented the true intention of Kaisheng Company, and its contents were consistent with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 203 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law) and did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. It was legally established and valid, and as an integral part of the original ceiling mortgage contract, it had the same legal effect as the original ceiling mortgage contract. Accordingly, the claims under the Small Enterprise Loan Contract of April 20, 2012, were included within the scope of the principal claims secured by the ceiling mortgage with a maximum amount of RMB 40,000,000. With regard to whether a corresponding modification registration for the ceiling mortgage is required for the matters stipulated in the Supplementary Agreement, the Property Law does not provide clear provisions, and the determination should be made in conjunction with the characteristics of ceiling mortgage and relevant legal provisions.

According to Paragraph 1 of Article 203 of the Property Law, a ceiling mortgage has two notable features: first, there is a definite maximum limit on the amount of claims secured by the ceiling mortgage, but the actual amount of claims incurred is uncertain; second, a ceiling mortgage provides security for claims that will occur continuously within a certain period. Therefore, the specific claims secured at the time of establishing the ceiling mortgage are generally not yet determined. Based on the principle of respecting party autonomy, Paragraph 2 of Article 203 of the Property Law makes a proviso to the preceding paragraph, allowing, with the consent of the parties, the inclusion of claims existing before the establishment of the ceiling mortgage into the scope of claims secured by the ceiling mortgage. However, this does not constitute a new establishment of a ceiling mortgage, nor is it a modification of the ceiling mortgage as provided in Article 205 of the Property Law. Similarly, according to Article 53 of the Measures for the Registration of Houses, the inclusion of claims existing before the establishment of a ceiling mortgage into the scope of claims secured by the ceiling mortgage is not a necessary item to be recorded in the mortgage certificate or the house register for the registration of the ceiling mortgage, and therefore it is not a statutory circumstance requiring an application for modification registration of the ceiling mortgage.

In this case, ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch and Kaisheng Company only entered into a supplementary agreement to include the claims existing before the establishment of the ceiling mortgage into the scope of claims secured by the ceiling mortgage. The amount of the included claims remained within the maximum limit of RMB 40,000,000 of the ceiling mortgage. The included fixed claims were not necessary items to be recorded in the mortgage certificate or the house register for the registration of the ceiling mortgage. Provided that no adverse effect is caused to other mortgagees, such autonomous act should be respected. Furthermore, according to the rules of commercial transactions, what is not prohibited by law is permissible. That is, when legal provisions are unclear, market transaction entities should not be burdened with the obligation to strictly follow transactional rules. Moreover, with regard to the inclusion of the claims under the loan contract of April 20, 2012, into the scope of claims secured by the ceiling mortgage, Kaisheng Company not only passed a shareholders' meeting resolution and issued a commitment letter for property mortgage guarantee, but also entered into the Supplementary Agreement with ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch, clearly including the existing loan claims within the scope of principal claims secured by the ceiling mortgage with a maximum amount of RMB 40,000,000. Now, Kaisheng Company's appeal arguing that the modification registration of the ceiling mortgage was necessary for the establishment of the mortgage under the Supplementary Agreement is not only lacking legal basis but also violates the principle of good faith.

In summary, ICBC Xuancheng Longshou Sub-branch and Kaisheng Company reached the Supplementary Agreement to include the claims under the loan contract of April 20, 2012, within the scope of principal claims secured by the aforementioned ceiling mortgage. Although no modification registration of the ceiling mortgage was made, the validity of the ceiling mortgage still extends to the claims under the included loan contract.

(Trial judges for the effective judgment: Tao Henghe, Wang Yusheng, Ma Shipeng)

Guiding Case No. 96

Song Wenjun v. Xi'an Dahua Catering Co., Ltd.

— dispute over confirmation of shareholder status

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on June 20, 2018)

Keywords: civil / confirmation of shareholder status / initial articles of association / restriction on equity transfer / repurchase

Ruling Gist

Where a state-owned enterprise is restructured into a limited liability company, and its initial articles of association impose restrictions on equity transfer, expressly providing for a company repurchase clause, such provisions may be deemed valid as long as they do not violate mandatory provisions of the Company Law or other laws. Where a limited liability company, in accordance with the provisions of its initial articles of association, repurchases a shareholder's equity for a reasonable consideration and reasonably disposes of it, such as by transferring it to other shareholders, the people's court shall uphold such actions.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 11, Paragraph 2 of Article 25, Article 35, and Article 74 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

Xi'an Dahua Catering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Dahua Company") was established on April 5, 1990. In May 2004, Dahua Company was restructured from a state-owned enterprise into a limited liability company. Song Wenjun, an employee of Dahua Company, contributed RMB 20,000 and became a natural person shareholder of Dahua Company. Article 14 of Chapter III "Registered Capital and Shares" of the Articles of Association of Dahua Company provides: "The company's equity shall not be sold or transferred to any group or individual outside the company. One year after the company's restructuring, with the approval of the board of directors, it may be donated, transferred, or inherited within the company. Upon the death or retirement of a shareholder, with the approval of the board of directors, the shares may be inherited, transferred, or acquired by the enterprise. If a shareholder resigns, is transferred out, is dismissed, or has their labor contract terminated, the shares must be retained upon departure, and the shares held shall be acquired by the enterprise..." Article 66 of Chapter XIII "Other Matters That Shareholders Deem Necessary to Provide" provides: "These Articles of Association are recognized by all shareholders and shall take effect from the date of the company's establishment." The articles of association were signed and passed by all shareholders of Dahua Company. On June 3, 2006, Song Wenjun filed a request with the company to terminate the labor contract and applied to withdraw the RMB 20,000 shares he held. On August 28, 2006, with the consent of Zhao Laisuo, the legal representative of Dahua Company, Song Wenjun received the full amount of the withdrawal of share capital, RMB 20,000. On January 8, 2007, Dahua Company held its 2006 annual general meeting of shareholders. The meeting had 107 shareholders expected to attend, with 104 shareholders actually attending, representing 93% of the total shares of the company. The meeting considered and approved the applications of three shareholders, Song Wenjun, Wang Peiqing, and Hang Chunguo, to withdraw their shares, and resolved that "their share capital shall be temporarily acquired and held by the company, and they shall not participate in the distribution of dividends." Subsequently, Song Wenjun, claiming that the buyback by Dahua Company violated legal provisions, failed to follow statutory procedures, and that the Company Law prohibits shareholders from illegally withdrawing capital contributions, requested a judicial confirmation of his shareholder status in Dahua Company.

Judgment

The Beilin District People's Court of Xi'an rendered a civil judgment on June 10, 2014, (2014) Bei Min Chu Zi No. 01339, ordering: The plaintiff Song Wenjun's claim for confirmation of his shareholder status in the defendant Xi'an Dahua Catering Co., Ltd. is dismissed. After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, Song Wenjun appealed. The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court issued a civil judgment on October 10, 2014, (2014) Xi Zhong Min Si Zhong Zi No. 00277, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. After the final judgment was pronounced, Song Wenjun, still dissatisfied, applied to the Shaanxi High People's Court for retrial. The Shaanxi High People's Court issued a civil ruling on March 25, 2015, (2014) Shan Min Er Shen Zi No. 00215, dismissing Song Wenjun's application for retrial.

Reasoning

The court in the effective judgment held: Upon hearing the reasons for the retrial application of the applicant for retrial, Song Wenjun, and the defense opinion of the respondent, Dahua Company, the issues in this case are as follows: 1. Whether the provision in the articles of association of Dahua Company regarding "shares must be retained upon departure" violates the prohibitive provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Company Law"), and whether such articles are valid; 2. Whether the buyback of Song Wenjun's equity by Dahua Company violates the relevant provisions of the Company Law, and whether Dahua Company constitutes an illegal withdrawal of capital contributions.

Regarding the first issue, first, Article 14 of the articles of association of Dahua Company provides: "The company's equity shall not be sold or transferred to any group or individual outside the company. One year after the company's restructuring, with the approval of the board of directors, it may be donated, transferred, or inherited within the company. Upon the death or retirement of a shareholder, with the approval of the board of directors, the shares may be inherited, transferred, or acquired by the enterprise. If a shareholder resigns, is transferred out, is dismissed, or has their labor contract terminated, the shares must be retained upon departure, and the shares held shall be acquired by the enterprise." In accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 25 of the Company Law, which provides that "shareholders shall sign or affix their seals on the company's articles of association," the articles of association of a limited liability company are a regulatory document unanimously agreed upon by all shareholders at the time of the company's establishment and binding on the company and all shareholders. Song Wenjun's act of signing the articles of association should be deemed as his recognition and consent to the aforementioned provisions, and such articles are binding on Dahua Company and Song Wenjun. Second, based on the characteristics of closedness and human union (people-oriented nature) of a limited liability company, certain restrictive provisions on the transfer of shares by shareholders set forth in the company's articles of association are an expression of corporate autonomy. In this case, when Dahua Company underwent enterprise restructuring, the reason Song Wenjun became a shareholder of Dahua Company was that Song Wenjun had a labor contract relationship with Dahua Company. If Song Wenjun had not established a labor relationship with Dahua Company, there would have been no possibility for Song Wenjun to become a shareholder of Dahua Company. Similarly, the provision in the articles of association of Dahua Company that takes the existence of a labor contract relationship with the company as the basis for acquiring shareholder status and consequently stipulates "shares must be retained upon departure" is consistent with the characteristics of closedness and human union of a limited liability company, is also an expression of the principle of corporate autonomy, and does not violate the prohibitive provisions of the Company Law. Third, the provisions on equity transfer in Article 14 of the articles of association of Dahua Company are restrictive provisions on the transfer of shares by shareholders, not prohibitive provisions. Song Wenjun's right to transfer his equity according to law is not prohibited by the company's articles of association, and there is no circumstance in which the articles of association of Dahua Company infringe upon Song Wenjun's right to transfer his equity. In summary, the courts of first instance and second instance both correctly determined that the articles of association of Dahua Company do not violate the prohibitive provisions of the Company Law and are valid. Song Wenjun's ground for retrial application in this regard cannot be established.

Regarding the second issue, the right to request a buyback by dissenting shareholders provided for in Article 74 of the Company Law has statutory conditions for exercise, namely, only in the following three circumstances: (1) the company has not distributed profits to shareholders for five consecutive years, although the company has been profitable for those five consecutive years and meets the conditions for distribution of profits provided by this Law; (2) the company merges, divides, or transfers its main property; (3) the term of business operation specified in the articles of association expires or other grounds for dissolution specified in the articles of association occur, and a resolution is adopted at a shareholders' meeting to modify the articles of association to continue the company. In such cases, dissenting shareholders have the right to demand that the company repurchase their equity, corresponding to the legal obligation of whether the company should fulfill the buyback of equity of dissenting shareholders. However, this case concerns whether Dahua Company has the right to repurchase Song Wenjun's equity based on the agreement in the company's articles of association and the mutual consensus with Song Wenjun, corresponding to whether Dahua Company has the right to repurchase Song Wenjun's equity. The nature of the two is different, and Article 74 of the Company Law is not applicable to this case. In this case, on June 3, 2006, Song Wenjun submitted an application to terminate the labor contract to Dahua Company and also wrote a "Share Withdrawal Application" on the same day, stating, "I request a full withdrawal of shares, and year-end profits or losses are not my concern." This "Share Withdrawal Application" should be considered as his true expression of intent. On August 28, 2006, Dahua Company refunded the full amount of his share capital, RMB 20,000, and on January 8, 2007, held a shareholders' meeting to consider and approve the share withdrawal applications of Song Wenjun and two other shareholders. Dahua Company, based on Song Wenjun's share withdrawal application and in accordance with the provisions of the company's articles of association, repurchased Song Wenjun's equity, and the procedure was not improper. In addition, the term "illegal withdrawal of capital contributions" as provided in the Company Law specifically refers to the act of a company's shareholder withdrawing its capital contribution to the company; a company cannot constitute the subject of an illegal withdrawal of capital contributions. Song Wenjun's ground for retrial application in this regard cannot be established. Accordingly, it is ruled that the retrial application of the applicant for retrial, Song Wenjun, is dismissed.

(Enforcement judges of the effective judgment: Wu Qiang, Pang Dong, Zhang Jie)
